title: Document that Quest-writing lore commands require an explicit actor declaration
description: LCLI-434 (Done) made lore fail closed when a Quest write (lore link/unlink, lore init --migrate-backlog's Quest apply/rollback path) has no explicit actor context declared, instead of silently attributing it to a hardcoded human identity. opum-cli-e2e qualified this against a real dev-tip build (opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#56) and found it is a breaking change for any existing caller that declares no actor: three of their own previously-passing harness rows started failing closed until they added harness-wide LORE_QUEST_ACTOR/LORE_QUEST_ACTOR_KIND/LORE_QUEST_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN env defaults. opum-agent confirmed and directed: the 0.5.0 CHANGELOG entry and lore instructions must say plainly that Quest-writing commands now require an actor declaration, and show the flags/env vars. Confirmed via 'lore link --help' and 'lore instructions' (grepped src/core/instructions.ts for 'actor'/'LORE_QUEST', zero matches) that neither surface currently documents this at all -- there is no CLI flag for actor context on lore link/unlink either, only the three env vars wired into src/adapters/quest.ts's resolveActor().

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 'linking' instructions topic (src/core/instructions.ts) documents that a Quest-backed bundle's lore link/unlink now requires LORE_QUEST_ACTOR/_ACTOR_KIND/_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN to be set, names the fail-closed behavior and error shape, and gives a concrete example
The existing LCLI-434 CHANGELOG.md entry (or a new entry) explicitly marks the actor requirement as BREAKING for existing callers, not just an attribution-quality improvement

docs/reference/cli-surface.md link/unlink rows (and the Backlog migration row, if it goes through the same adapter path) are checked for the same gap and updated if they describe exit codes without mentioning the new fail-closed actor requirement

implementationNotes: Scope expanded per opum-agent's ruling: rather than just documenting the drift-vs-validation inconsistency, fixed it at the source since 0.5.0 is already the breaking release. Verified via full source trace (not just opum-cli-e2e's initial claim, which itself had one error I caught and one correction I verified back) that lore link/unlink folded a missing-actor failure into LORE-58's generic per-task drift wrapper (src/commands/link.ts's backRefFailure), while lore init --migrate-backlog's Quest apply/rollback path already surfaced it unwrapped as validation. Fix: added isQuestActorContextFailure() to src/adapters/quest.ts (stable discriminator over all three resolveActor() rejection codes, gave the actor-kind-invalid case a code for consistency with the other two) and a shared actorContextFailure() helper in link.ts that re-throws the original validation error directly, bypassing backRefFailure, when any per-task outcome failed for this reason -- genuine per-task drift still goes through the wrapper unchanged. Also improved all three resolveActor() error hints to show a concrete, copy-pasteable env-var example instead of referencing a non-existent CLI flag (confirmed via 'lore link --help' that no such flag exists). Added regression tests asserting the top-level error_type for all four commands (link, unlink, migrate-backlog apply, migrate-backlog rollback) all now uniformly report validation. Updated the 'linking' instructions topic, cli-surface.md's link/unlink/init exit tables, and the CHANGELOG's LCLI-434 entry to describe the single unified shape. Full verification: bun test 2889/2889, typecheck clean, lint clean, lore check clean.
